cues.zh: 四十五年前，阿波罗8号宇航员弗兰克·博尔曼、吉姆·洛弗尔和比尔·安德斯成为首批绕月飞行的人类，
cues.en: Forty-five years ago, Apollo 8 astronauts Frank Borman, Jim Lovell, and Bill Anders became the first humans to orbit the Moon,

cues.zh: 也是首批目睹“地出”壮丽景象的人。
cues.en: and the first to witness the magnificent sight called "Earthrise."

cues.zh: 如今，我们首次能够以宇航员当时的视角，精确重现这一历史性时刻，
cues.en: Now, for the first time, we can see this historic event exactly as the astronauts saw it,

cues.zh: 这得益于NASA月球勘测轨道飞行器（LRO）的新数据。
cues.en: thanks to new data from NASA's Lunar Reconnaissance Orbiter, or LRO.

cues.zh: LRO出色的全球月球地图，结合宇航员自己拍摄的照片，
cues.en: LRO's superb global lunar maps, combined with the astronauts' own photographs,

cues.zh: 揭示了阿波罗8号当时位于月球上空的哪个位置，甚至其在太空中的精确朝向，
cues.en: reveal where Apollo 8 was over the Moon, and even its precise orientation in space,

cues.zh: 也就是宇航员首次看到地球从月球荒芜地平线上升起的时刻。
cues.en: when the astronauts first saw the Earth rising above the Moon's barren horizon.

cues.zh: 1968年12月24日，休斯敦时间上午10点30分刚过几分钟，
cues.en: On December 24, 1968, a few minutes after 10:30 am Houston time,

cues.zh: 阿波罗8号第四次从月球背面绕出。
cues.en: Apollo 8 was coming around from the far side of the Moon for the fourth time.

cues.zh: 指令长 Frank Borman 坐在左侧驾驶席，正准备按照飞行计划调整飞船姿态。
cues.en: Mission Commander Frank Borman was in the left-hand seat, preparing to turn the spacecraft to a new orientation according to the flight plan.

cues.zh: 领航员 Jim Lovell 在飞船的下层设备舱，正准备用机载六分仪对月表地标进行观测，
cues.en: Navigator Jim Lovell was in the spacecraft's lower equipment bay, about to make sightings on lunar landmarks with the onboard sextant,

cues.zh: 而 Bill Anders 坐在右侧驾驶席，正透过侧窗观察月球，
cues.en: and Bill Anders was in the right-hand seat, observing the Moon through his side window,

cues.zh: 并用一台装有 250 毫米长焦镜头的 Hasselblad 相机拍照。
cues.en: and taking pictures with a Hasselblad still camera, fitted with a 250-mm telephoto lens.

cues.zh: 与此同时，另一台装有 80 毫米镜头的 Hasselblad 安装在 Borman 正前方的窗户上——也就是所谓的对接窗，
cues.en: Meanwhile, a second Hasselblad with an 80-mm lens was mounted in Borman's front-facing window, the so-called rendezvous window,

cues.zh: 通过自动定时器拍摄月球：每二十秒自动拍摄一张。
cues.en: photographing the Moon on an automatic timer: a new picture every twenty seconds.

cues.zh: 结合 LRO 的高分辨率地形图分析，这些照片表明，当飞船看到地球升起时，Borman 仍在调整 Apollo 8 的姿态。
cues.en: These photographs, matched with LRO's high resolution terrain maps, show that Borman was still turning Apollo 8 when the Earth appeared.

cues.zh: 正是由于这次转向的时机，
cues.en: It was only because of the timing of this rotation that the Earthrise,

cues.zh: 此前三圈绕月飞行中，阿波罗 8 号宇航员都没能看到地出；这一次，它出现在比尔·安德斯侧窗的视野里。
cues.en: which had happened on Apollo 8's three previous orbits, but was unseen by the astronauts, now came into view in Bill Anders's side window.

cues.zh: 这是根据月球勘测轨道飞行器（LRO）的数据，由戈达德科学可视化工作室重现的画面。
cues.en: Here's what it looked like, as recreated from LRO data by Goddard's Scientific Visualization Studio.

cues.zh: 你会听到阿波罗 8 号机载录音机录下的宇航员声音，
cues.en: You'll hear the astronauts' voices as captured by Apollo 8's onboard tape recorder,

cues.zh: 先是弗兰克·博尔曼宣布开始滚转机动，
cues.en: beginning with Frank Borman announcing the start of the roll maneuver,

cues.zh: 接着，随着阿波罗 8 号转向，你会看到升起的地球从一扇舷窗移到另一扇舷窗。
cues.en: and you'll see the rising Earth move from one window to another as Apollo 8 turns.

cues.zh: 对宇航员来说，看到地出是一次意料之外、令人振奋的经历，
cues.en: For the astronauts, seeing the Earthrise was an unexpected and electrifying experience,

cues.zh: 比尔·安德斯拍下的三张照片中，有一张成为了 20 世纪的经典影像。
cues.en: and one of the three photographs taken by Bill Anders became an iconic image of the 20th century.

cues.zh: 但正如我们刚才所见所闻，那张照片其实是团队合作的结晶：
cues.en: But as we've just seen and heard, that photograph was actually a group effort:

cues.zh: 不仅因为 Jim Lovell 找到了那卷彩色胶卷并交给了 Anders，
cues.en: not just because Jim Lovell found the roll of color film and gave it to Anders,

cues.zh: 更因为如果不是 Frank Borman 刚好在那时调整飞船朝向，宇航员们根本就看不到地球升起。
cues.en: but because the astronauts wouldn't have seen the Earth if Frank Borman hadn't been turning the spacecraft just as it was coming up.

cues.zh: 如今，“地出”已经成为人类历史上最伟大探索之一的象征，
cues.en: Today, the Earthrise has become a symbol of one of history's greatest explorations,

cues.zh: 象征着人类首次启程前往另一个世界，并在回望时，
cues.en: when humans first journeyed to another world and then, looking back,

cues.zh: 借用 Lovell 的话，看到了我们的母星——这片浩瀚太空中壮丽的绿洲。
cues.en: saw their home planet, in Lovell's words, as a grand oasis in the vastness of space.

cues.zh: 我是 Andrew Chaikin，《A Man on the Moon》的作者。
cues.en: I'm Andrew Chaikin, author of "A Man on the Moon."
